architecture: Batched deep ensemble of 4 pre-LN residual MLPs (Linear 14->768, 6 blocks LN-Linear-GELU-Linear width 768 with zero-init output projections, LN, Linear 768->2001 with zero-init weights and bias 0.5), run as one baddbmm per layer. Exact V4 resonator-permutation symmetry: each member trains on the full 4-view orbit, and the output is averaged over members and views. Fused AdamW, batch 32, lr 7e-4, wd 1e-2, grad clip 1, EMA 0.999, time-aware cosine (400 warmup steps), MSE on raw y, minmax x.
insight: Adding the global angle-flip (negating all four thetas) to the exact V4 symmetry lowered val MSE from 6.51e-3 to 5.67e-3 (-13%). With identical seed and batch order, the flip run was lower at every checkpoint from epoch 50, so the flip looks like a real mirror symmetry; treat the 8-element group as valid. Both ensembles memorize the training set (train MSE about 1e-6) and val MSE bottoms out near epoch 220 of about 600, so the next MLP step should add regularization (dropout, stronger weight decay, input noise) rather than more epochs or capacity.

architecture: Same 4-member batched pre-LN residual-MLP ensemble (width 768, depth 6) and recipe as v4ens (AdamW batch 32, lr 7e-4, wd 1e-2, clip 1, EMA 0.999, time-aware cosine, raw-y MSE). Adds one change: the symmetry group is V4 x global angle flip (negate all four thetas, a mirror under x/y polarization), giving 8 views. Training uses the full 8-view orbit, and the output is averaged over members and the 8 views.
insight: Adding the global angle-flip (negating all four thetas) to the exact V4 symmetry lowered val MSE from 6.51e-3 to 5.67e-3 (-13%). architecture: V4-exact relational transformer: 1 (h,p) token + 4 resonator tokens from one shared GELU-MLP embedding of raw (rx, ry, theta, sin/cos 2theta, (rx-ry)cos/sin 2theta, rx+ry, h, p); 3 pre-LN blocks (d 256, 8 heads, FFN 4x) with learned per-head attention-logit biases indexed by the pair relation i XOR j, so outputs are exactly invariant to the sub-cell-shift permutations; concat(global, mean resonator token) then 2x1024 GELU MLP then Linear(2001). y global_standard, MSE, AdamW lr 8.5e-4, wd 0.05 (none on norms/biases), batch 64, dropout 0.1, time-aware cosine with about 300 warmup steps, grad clip 1, EMA about 0.996.
insight: At k=500 the V4-exact relation-biased transformer fits the train split to about 2e-5 while val MSE plateaus at 5.2-5.4e-3 from epoch ~150 on. The bottleneck is generalisation, not optimisation: steps are launch-bound at ~16 ms, giving about 1100-1400 epochs in 180 s. Raw (rx, ry, theta) inputs gave the run-1 model 2.1e-3 MSE on its own training rows when the ellipses at theta = +-pi/4 were re-encoded as (ry, rx, -theta), which is the same physical ellipse. Switching to shape-tensor invariant features (s, u, v) removed this exactly and gave 5.33e-3 -> 5.02e-3 (-6%, best epoch 125, plateau median 5.36e-3 -> 5.20e-3), which is within k=500 noise.

architecture: Improve of r00_draft2_v4tf with one change, the resonator token features: ellipse shape-tensor invariants s = rx+ry, u, v = (rx-ry)cos/sin 2theta, |d| = sqrt(u^2+v^2+0.01), u/|d|, v/|d|, plus h, p. The two encodings of the same ellipse, (rx, ry, +-pi/4) and (ry, rx, -+pi/4), now give identical outputs. Everything else is unchanged: V4-exact relation-biased transformer (3 blocks, d 256, 8 heads), mean pool, 2x1024 MLP head, global_standard y, MSE, AdamW lr 8.5e-4, wd 0.05, batch 64, dropout 0.1, time-aware cosine, grad clip 1, EMA.
insight: At k=500 the V4-exact relation-biased transformer fits the train split to about 2e-5 while val MSE plateaus at 5.2-5.4e-3 from epoch ~150 on. Raw (rx, ry, theta) inputs gave the run-1 model 2.1e-3 MSE on its own training rows when the ellipses at theta = +-pi/4 were re-encoded as (ry, rx, -theta), which is the same physical ellipse. Switching to shape-tensor invariant features (s, u, v) removed this exactly and gave 5.33e-3 -> 5.02e-3 (-6%, best epoch 125, plateau median 5.36e-3 -> 5.20e-3), which is within k=500 noise.

architecture: V4 orbit-averaged residual-MLP encoder (14->512, 3 pre-LN GELU blocks with hidden 1024; latent averaged over the 4 resonator double transpositions) + hybrid structured decoder: rank-64 learned basis head plus a FiLM-conditioned ConvTranspose1d decoder (128x32 seed map up to 64ch x 256, residual Conv1d k=5 blocks) with a zero-init sub-pixel x8 head to 2048 points, cropped to 2001; MSE on globally standardised y, fused AdamW lr 1.4e-3, wd 1e-2 on matrices only, batch 64, time-aware cosine over 180 s (warmup 10 ep), grad clip 1.0, no dropout or EMA. Best epoch 32 of 1283; plateau val about 6.99e-3.
insight: At k=500 the train set is memorised within about 100 epochs and the best checkpoint is an early high-LR validation dip. Keeping the decoder fixed and swapping the orbit-averaged 14-input MLP encoder for a shared per-resonator token MLP plus V4 pair-partition (12|34, 13|24, 14|23) relational sums cut val MSE by 16% (5.98e-3 -> 5.04e-3; plateau 6.99e-3 -> 5.82e-3). So at small k the encoder's weight sharing sets accuracy, and the basis plus transposed-conv sub-pixel decoder can only show its value at larger k. It is also about 2x cheaper per step than interpolate+conv to full 2048 resolution, which is launch-overhead-bound on this Windows GPU.

architecture: Improve of symconv, encoder only: pairwise-relational V4-invariant encoder. A shared resonator-token MLP phi maps [rx_i, ry_i, theta_i, h, p] to 256 (2 residual blocks). A pair MLP psi acts on [u_a+u_b, u_a*u_b] plus a partition-type embedding and is summed over the 12|34, 13|24 and 14|23 partitions. rho takes [sum u, Q_A, Q_B, Q_C, h, p] to 512 (2 residual blocks) -> z. Decoder and training are unchanged: rank-64 basis plus FiLM transposed-conv sub-pixel decoder, MSE on global-standardised y, fused AdamW lr 1.4e-3, wd 1e-2, batch 64, time-aware cosine over 180 s, grad clip 1. Best epoch 45 of 1274; plateau val about 5.82e-3.
insight: At k=500 the train set is memorised within about 100 epochs and the best checkpoint is an early high-LR validation dip. So at small k the encoder's weight sharing sets accuracy, and the basis plus transposed-conv sub-pixel decoder can only show its value at larger k. architecture: Improve of r05, one change: a batched deep ensemble of M=4 independently initialised copies of the r05 V4-exact relational transformer (shape-tensor resonator tokens, 4 pre-LN blocks d320/8 heads with relation biases, mean pool, 2x1536 GELU MLP head -> 2001). Members run as stacked (M,...) batched matmuls, each is trained on its own MSE (loss = mean of member MSEs), and the output is the member mean. Recipe is r05's: global_standard y, AdamW lr 1.5e-3, wd 0.01, batch 256, dropout 0.02, time-aware cosine, EMA 0.998935. The only recipe difference is a global grad clip of 1/sqrt(M)=0.5. Best epoch 78 of 512.
insight: A batched 4-member ensemble of the incumbent lowered val MSE at k=16000 from 1.722e-3 to 1.510e-3 (-12%) for about 1.3x the step cost. Members disagree by only 2.5e-4 at random geometries (label-free check), so about 1.43e-3 of the error is shared across seeds and M=8 would gain only about 3%. A shared-renderer patch head without attention reached only 1.599e-3 (-7%), so the 8.3e-4 of r06_explore_patchxattn comes from patch self- and cross-attention, not from weight-shared rendering alone. Also, the incumbent has already learned the global angle-flip symmetry (prediction change 3.5e-5), so flip symmetrization is not worth a run.

architecture: Improve of r05, one change: the spectral head. The r05 encoder is unchanged. The MLP head is replaced by a shared-renderer patch head with no attention: trunk Linear(640->1536)-GELU-Linear(1536->32x128) patch codes plus a learned patch position embedding, then 2 pre-LN GELU MLP blocks (128->512->128) shared by all patches, LayerNorm, and one shared Linear(128->128) renderer, overlap-added at stride 64 and centre-cropped 2112->2001. Recipe is r05's: global_standard y, AdamW lr 1.5e-3, wd 0.01, batch 256, dropout 0.02, time-aware cosine, EMA 0.998935, grad clip 1. Single model, best epoch 65 of 450.
insight: A batched 4-member ensemble of the incumbent lowered val MSE at k=16000 from 1.722e-3 to 1.510e-3 (-12%) for about 1.3x the step cost. Members disagree by only 2.5e-4 at random geometries (label-free check), so about 1.43e-3 of the error is shared across seeds and M=8 would gain only about 3%. A shared-renderer patch head without attention reached only 1.599e-3 (-7%), so the 8.3e-4 of r06_explore_patchxattn comes from patch self- and cross-attention, not from weight-shared rendering alone. Also, the incumbent has already learned the global angle-flip symmetry (prediction change 3.5e-5), so flip symmetrization is not worth a run.

architecture: Encoder-decoder transformer with a spectral patch-query decoder instead of an MLP head. 5 geometry tokens (global h,p + 4 resonators with ellipse shape-tensor features) pass 2 pre-LN blocks with V4-relation logit biases, so the output is exactly V4-invariant. 32 patch query tokens (S=64; learned position embedding + pooled-latent projection) pass 4 decoder blocks [patch self-attention with ALiBi-initialised relative-position bias, cross-attention to the geometry tokens, GELU FFN 4x]. A shared Linear(d->2S) renders each patch, overlap-added and cropped to 2001 points, plus a per-point bias. d 256, 8 heads, 6.2M params. Training: global_standard y, MSE, random all-angle sign-flip augmentation, AdamW lr 1e-3, batch 256, wd 0.05, betas (0.9, 0.98), time-aware cosine with 500-step warmup, grad clip 1, EMA, dropout 0.1, bf16 autocast.
insight: At k=16000, swapping the incumbent's 2x1536 MLP head for an attention decoder cut val MSE from 1.72e-3 to 8.3e-4 with S=64 patches and to 6.6e-4 with S=32 patches, at 6.2M params; in that decoder, spectral patch tokens cross-attend to the V4-invariant geometry tokens and to each other, and one linear renderer is shared across all patches. The S=32 run was better at every matched epoch, and the gain came mostly from mid-scale resonance structure, while the sharpest narrow peaks remain the main residual (54% of squared error sits at the 10% steepest points); a checkpoint diagnostic showed the incumbent had already learned the angle-flip symmetry (averaging flipped predictions gained only 0.5%).

architecture: Improve of r06_explore_patchxattn with one change: finer spectral patches, S=32 (63 patch query tokens, renderer Linear(d->64), overlap-add stride 32). Otherwise identical: V4-relation-biased 5-token geometry encoder (2 blocks), 4-block patch decoder [self-attention with relative-position bias, cross-attention to the geometry tokens, FFN 4x], d 256, 8 heads, 6.2M params. Training: global_standard y, MSE, flip augmentation, AdamW lr 1e-3, batch 256, wd 0.05, time-aware cosine, clip 1, EMA, dropout 0.1, bf16.
insight: At k=16000, swapping the incumbent's 2x1536 MLP head for an attention decoder cut val MSE from 1.72e-3 to 8.3e-4 with S=64 patches and to 6.6e-4 with S=32 patches, at 6.2M params; in that decoder, spectral patch tokens cross-attend to the V4-invariant geometry tokens and to each other, and one linear renderer is shared across all patches. The S=32 run was better at every matched epoch, and the gain came mostly from mid-scale resonance structure, while the sharpest narrow peaks remain the main residual (54% of squared error sits at the 10% steepest points); a checkpoint diagnostic showed the incumbent had already learned the angle-flip symmetry (averaging flipped predictions gained only 0.5%).

architecture: Batched deep ensemble K=4 of the incumbent V4-exact relational transformer (shape-tensor resonator tokens, d 320, 4 pre-LN blocks, 8 heads, relation-biased attention, mean pool, 2x1536 MLP head), each member trained on its own MSE, output = member mean; recipe change: effective AdamW weight decay from a decay timescale (wd 0.01 -> 0.1015, tau ~6.6k steps); lr 1.5e-3, batch 256, dropout 0.02, EMA 0.99894, global clip 0.5 (1 per member), time-aware cosine, global_standard y, MSE; best epoch 75 of 292
insight: On the incumbent family the training recipe is not the bottleneck: making AdamW weight decay effective (0.01 -> 0.10, decay timescale 67k -> 6.6k steps) left a 4-member ensemble at 1.503e-3 (vs 1.510e-3 for r06_improve_ens4; same best epoch ~75 and the same slow rise afterwards, even with the LR annealed to its floor), SAM (rho 0.1) made it 21% worse (1.824e-3), and the incumbent is already invariant to the global angle flip to 3.5e-5 MSE at unlabeled geometries, so flip augmentation or test-time flipping can gain <1%. The remaining error is systematic and shared by the ensemble members (about 82% error correlation), so further gains have to come from the output parameterization (frequency-shared decoders such as r06_explore_patchxattn at 8.3e-4), not from regularization or the schedule.

architecture: Same K=4 batched ensemble and recipe as r06_recipe_ens4wd (wd 0.1015) plus sharpness-aware minimisation: per-member perturbation rho 0.1 along the member gradient, gradient taken at the perturbed point, perturbation undone by an AdamW pre-step hook (2 forward/backward passes per step); best epoch 78 of 157

architecture: Improve of r06_explore_patchxattn_s32 with one change: DiT-style adaLN in the decoder. One zero-weight Linear on SiLU(pooled geometry latent) gives per-block shift/scale/gate for the 3 decoder sub-layers plus shift/scale for the final norm, initialised as identity so the net starts as the parent function. Otherwise identical: V4-relation-biased 5-token encoder (2 blocks), 4 S=32 patch decoder blocks (self-attn with rel-pos bias, cross-attn, FFN 4x), d 256, 8 heads, 8.66M params. Recipe: global_standard y, MSE, flip aug, AdamW lr 1e-3, bs 256, wd 0.05, time-aware cosine, clip 1, EMA, dropout 0.1, bf16. Step cost ~1.2x the parent; 157 epochs in 720 s.
insight: At k=16000 neither refinement beat the S=32 patch-decoder parent (6.63e-4). adaLN conditioning of every decoder sub-layer reached 7.27e-4 and S=16 patches reached 7.45e-4; both were also worse at equal epochs (7.53e-4 each at epoch 100 vs 7.19e-4 for the parent, despite a lower LR), so the S64->S32 gain does not continue to S=16, and multiplicative geometry conditioning only adds step cost (1.2x and 1.9x) under the 720 s budget, so the parent remains the best node.

architecture: Improve of r06_explore_patchxattn_s32 with one change: finer spectral patches, S=16 (126 patch query tokens, shared renderer Linear(d->32), overlap-add stride 16, ALiBi slopes rescaled to keep the parent's locality in frequency points). Otherwise identical: V4-relation-biased 5-token encoder (2 blocks), 4 patch decoder blocks (self-attn with rel-pos bias, cross-attn to geometry tokens, FFN 4x), d 256, 8 heads, 6.18M params. Same recipe as the parent (global_standard y, MSE, flip aug, AdamW lr 1e-3, bs 256, wd 0.05, time-aware cosine, clip 1, EMA, dropout 0.1, bf16). Step cost ~1.9x the parent; 113 epochs in 720 s.
insight: At k=16000 neither refinement beat the S=32 patch-decoder parent (6.63e-4). adaLN conditioning of every decoder sub-layer reached 7.27e-4 and S=16 patches reached 7.45e-4; both were also worse at equal epochs (7.53e-4 each at epoch 100 vs 7.19e-4 for the parent, despite a lower LR), so the S64->S32 gain does not continue to S=16, and multiplicative geometry conditioning only adds step cost (1.2x and 1.9x) under the 720 s budget, so the parent remains the best node.

architecture: Parent r06_explore_patchxattn_s32 unchanged (V4-relation-biased 5-token geometry encoder, 2 blocks + 4-block patch decoder [rel-pos self-attn, cross-attn to geometry, FFN 4x], S=32 / 63 patch queries, overlap-add renderer, d 256, 8 heads) with ONE change: batch 128 instead of 256 at the same AdamW lr 1e-3; wd 0.05, dropout 0.1, betas (0.9, 0.98), EMA, time-aware cosine, clip 1, bf16, flip aug, global_standard y, MSE. Got 65 epochs (7.4k steps) under heavy GPU contention.
insight: Compared with the parent's curve at equal epochs, none of the three one-change refinements helps. Dropout 0 overfits: val bottoms at 9.88e-4 at epoch 65, then rises 14% while train loss halves. lr 2e-3 trails the parent at every epoch: 8.84e-4 after 105 fully annealed epochs vs the parent's 7.11e-4 at epoch 105 mid-schedule. Batch 128 matches the parent per epoch but is worse per step (8.50e-4 vs 6.86e-4 at 7.4k steps), and steps are launch-bound (about 23 ms each from batch 64 to 256), so it also costs more wall time. The parent's batch 256 / lr 1e-3 / dropout 0.1 stay, and the next refinement should try more regularisation (dropout 0.15-0.2). The parent (r06_explore_patchxattn_s32, 6.63e-4) remains the round's best. All three runs shared the GPU with each other and a game (6.5-10.9 s/epoch vs the parent's 3.0, so 65-107 epochs instead of 229), so their absolute val MSEs are not directly comparable to the parent's.
